text:
maya: heads-up: after today's autoscheduler + autobatch merge we've seen multiple canary OOMs. memory climbs steadily for seqlen ~4096, reproducer attached.

sam: CI link: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/longctx/1234 — job fails with OOM at ~1m20s into the run. perf/regression alert from ci-bot.

leo: starting a quick bisect now. my hunch: PR #7892 changed the eviction score to include age*size which may be starving compact heuristics when autobatch increases inflight KV windows. reproducer command: `./run_infer --model rwd-open-7b --seq-len 4096 --batch 8 --trace-kv`

maya: quick local trace (snip):
```
KVCache: total_backing=18.3G slab_used=15.8G free_slab=0.9G
evict_scores: hot_slab=0.12 cold_slab=0.78 age_factor=1.9
alloc_map: heaplet_count=48 slab_frag_ratio=0.72
```
looks like slab reuse drops and small pagelets pile up.

ci-bot: perf/regression detected: benchmark longctx-512 memory_peak +18% (baseline 6.2G -> 7.3G), p95 latency unchanged. See artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/artifacts/1234/mem-profile.pb.gz

rahul: can toggle the autobatch heuristic flag on canary to confirm interaction. maya — can you try `--autobatch=off` on the reproducer and post memory trace?

maya: tried that — with autobatch disabled the backing store stabilizes (~8.0G) and slab_frag_ratio drops to 0.34. so autobatch *plus* the new evict scoring looks like the interaction.

sam: bisect update: reverting PR #7892 on a canary node immediately prevents the OOM reproduction. reapply the PR and OOM returns. so PR is a likely root cause, but only when autobatch is enabled (so two-factor).

leo: stack excerpt from crash profile (addr masked):
```
#0 0x7fffa1 alloc_slab()
#1 0x7fffa2 kv_alloc_pagelet()
#2 0x7fffa3 batch_dispatch_fastpath()
#3 0x7fffa4 kernel_select_and_dispatch()
```
suggests allocation hotspot in batch fastpath.

maya: telemetry: /kv/frag_ratio spiked to 0.78 on canary hosts right after the rollout, and heaplet_reserve_free went nearly to zero. also saw kernel_selector fastpath fallbacks increase 3x.

rahul: plan proposal: 1) pause rollout (pin previous stable), 2) hot-revert PR #7892 on canary fleet, 3) add integration test that simulates skewed seqlen distribution + autobatch to catch fragmentation leaks, 4) investigate improving evict scoring to account for inflight batch windows.

sam: +1 to that. I can push the revert and a failing test. also adding a short-term telemetry check to alert when slab_frag_ratio > 0.6.

leo: follow-up todo: run pprof heap before/after revert and compare flamegraphs, and instrument the kernel-selector path to emit kv-alloc site labels. I'll also look at whether kernel selection changed per-request sequence-length estimates and caused suboptimal pagelet packing.

deploy-bot: Started rollback: release rwd-infer-2026.03.18-canary -> pinned to rwd-infer-2026.03.17. Job id 54892.

maya: thanks. if anyone can take the bisect logs and pair them with the telemetry for the affected instances (i-0a12, i-0b34) that'd speed up root-cause. adding @rahul @leo to postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
